title: Budgets, alerts, cost allocation tags and Cost Explorer

videos.script: A bill on AWS is not a surprise because the prices are hidden. It is a surprise because nobody was watching it. {{bill}} This lesson builds the three instruments that watch. The first is a budget. {{budget}} A budget is a number and a few thresholds. When spending crosses one, somebody gets a message. That is all it does. It never switches anything off. {{alerts}} It has two kinds of alert. One says the money is already spent. The other says the month is heading over, days before it happens. {{tags}} The second instrument is a tag, a label on each resource. Without tags, the bill knows which service cost money, but not whose it was. {{gates}} And a tag only counts on the bill once it is switched on in Billing. Even then, it labels new costs, not old ones. {{explorer}} The third is Cost Explorer, which asks the bill a question. Which team, which service, which month. {{moto}} Your lab has no bill, because moto charges nothing. So you will build the budget and the tags for real, and ask the questions against an empty answer. Every price comes from AWS's own list. {{end}}
